extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and practicing writers, creative writers and authors
extracted.subtask_description: A compact list of practical craft, career, and voice-focused tips for writers to produce stronger, more authentic, and more impactful work across genres. Emphasizes purpose, pacing, honesty, and professional behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't Let Anyone Pigeonhole Your Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Storytelling is storytelling — resist being boxed into a single genre or label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write across genres if that is where your story or voice leads; avoid letting others' expectations limit what you create. Anti-pattern: restricting yourself because others insist you 'should' only write one thing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose Who You Want to Become on the Page
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide intentionally what voice, persona, or presence you will adopt in your writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the page to amplify an authentic voice; be deliberate about the version of yourself you present in your work rather than writing passively or by accident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribute to the Political Climate
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and use writing as a form of activism or civic engagement when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how your work affects political conversations and take responsibility for engaging with social issues if that aligns with your aims. Guidance implies using writing to influence or reflect on political contexts rather than treating writing as apolitical by default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Writing to Make Others Care
rubrics_metrics.description: Help readers understand the world through your perspective — make them care about your subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft pieces that translate your concerns into empathy or understanding for readers; prioritize clarity of perspective and emotional resonance so the audience connects with the material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide What You Want to Accomplish
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify your purpose before you begin writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define the objective of a piece (what you want it to do or achieve) up front so decisions during drafting serve that purpose. Anti-pattern: writing without an aim and ending up unfocused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Selective About What to Include
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrow your focus to one or two ideas; favor depth over breadth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trim extraneous material and concentrate on a small number of central ideas to explore them thoroughly. Scoring note: stronger pieces typically show concentrated development rather than trying to cover too much.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on Propulsion
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain steady pacing and forward movement to keep audiences engaged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure sentences, scenes, and sections so the reader feels compelled to continue; avoid stagnant passages that stall the narrative or argument. Example principle: prioritize momentum in craft decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creatively Multitask
rubrics_metrics.description: Work on multiple projects and switch tasks when you are blocked on one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use productive switching to sustain output and creativity: when stalled on a project, move to another rather than waiting for inspiration. Anti-pattern: abandoning writing entirely when encountering a single block.

rubrics_metrics.name: Win Fairly
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge opposing viewpoints and present their strongest counter-arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage honestly with critics and alternatives; strengthen your position by addressing the best versions of opposing ideas rather than straw-manning them. Ethical/professional guidance for persuasive writing and public discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show Your Work
rubrics_metrics.description: Display the reasoning, process, or evidence that led you to your conclusions instead of merely asserting them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build credibility and reader trust by revealing how you arrived at claims — include context, steps of thinking, and supporting detail. Anti-pattern: making declarative statements without backing or demonstration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set the Right Type of Goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize skill-building and internal development over external, outcome-based goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus goals on practicing and improving craft rather than solely on publication, awards, or other external validations. This framing supports long-term growth versus short-term metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask for What You Want
rubrics_metrics.description: Be explicit and public about your aspirations and what you hope to achieve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request opportunities, state your aims, and make your ambitions known rather than expecting others to infer them. Career-development tip: visibility and clear requests can create openings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't Dim Your Light for Others
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not minimize your confidence, achievements, or voice to make others more comfortable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remain unapologetic about your strengths and presence; avoid self-effacement intended to soothe others. Ethical/social guidance: protect your creative identity and confidence even when it unsettles some peers.
